english: The teacher listens hurriedly.
tip: The -yle on aceleyle turns the noun acele (haste) into an adverb: with haste, hurriedly.

english: I walk home from school.
tip: yürüyerek adds -yerek to yürü (walk) to mean 'by walking'; -erek shows the manner of an action.

english: Toward evening the weather cooled down.
tip: doğru means 'toward' and follows a dative noun: akşam takes -a, giving akşama doğru = toward evening.

english: I went instead of my mother.
tip: yerine = 'instead of' and needs the genitive: annem + -in gives annemin yerine = in place of my mother.

english: While crossing the bridge we watched the sea.
tip: The -ken on geçerken means 'while': geç (cross) + -erken = while crossing, happening at the same time.

english: Cars waited a long time in traffic.
tip: Arabalar is plural but the verb stays singular: bekledi, not beklediler. Non-human plural subjects take a singular verb.

english: I forgot to take my medicine this morning.
tip: unutmak takes the verbal noun in -mayı: al (take) + -mayı = almayı, so almayı unuttum = I forgot to take.

english: Every Sunday we have breakfast as a family.
tip: ailece adds -ce to aile (family) to mean 'as a family, all together'; -ce marks doing something collectively.

english: He sends an email to his boss every morning.
tip: gönderir is the aorist (-ir), used for habits: with her sabah it means 'sends every morning', not right now.

english: When I go to the market I write a list of things to buy.
tip: gittiğimde means 'when I go': git + -tiğimde. The -diğimde ending marks 'when someone does something'.

target: Bu müzede çok ilginç eserler sergileniyor.
english: Very interesting works are exhibited in this museum.
tip: sergileniyor is passive: sergile (exhibit) + -n- = 'is exhibited'. The -n- makes the action happen to the subject.

target: Çocukların dışarıda daha çok oynamasını istiyorum.
english: I want the children to play outside more.
tip: To want someone else to act, use -masını istemek: oyna + -masını = oynamasını, with çocukların in the genitive.

target: Okulun yanında büyük bir market var.
english: There is a big market next to the school.
tip: yanında (next to) needs the genitive on the noun: okul + -un = okulun yanında = next to the school.

target: Kütüphanedeki kitaplar alfabetik sıraya göre dizilmiş.
english: The books in the library are arranged in alphabetical order.
tip: kütüphanedeki adds -ki to the locative: kütüphanede (in the library) + -ki = 'the ones in the library'.

target: Bu oyuncak çocuğum için çok pahalı geldi.
english: This toy seemed too expensive for my child.
tip: Here geldi (from gelmek, to come) means 'seemed': pahalı geldi = came across as expensive, not literally arrived.

target: Eskiden burada bir göl varmış ama kurumuş.
english: There used to be a lake here but it dried up.
tip: varmış adds -mış for reported or inferred facts: 'there used to be, apparently'. It marks things you did not witness.

target: Keşke kitap okumak için daha çok zamanım olsa.
english: I wish I had more time to read books.
tip: keşke pairs with the conditional -sa for a wish: olsa = 'if only there were', so keşke ... olsa = I wish.

english: We picked apples from the tree.
tip: ağaçtan uses the ablative -tan = 'from': ağaç + -tan = from the tree. It marks the source of the action.

english: I can cook traditional Turkish dishes.
tip: yapabilirim shows ability with -abil: yap (do) + -abil + -irim = 'I can make'. -abil means 'be able to'.

english: According to the agreement, payment will be made tomorrow.
tip: göre (according to) follows a dative noun: anlaşma + -ya = anlaşmaya göre = according to the agreement.

english: The doctor said I should take the medicine regularly.
tip: almalıymış is built on -malı = must/should: al + -malı = 'should take'. -malı expresses necessity.

target: Otobüs trafik sıkışıklığı yüzünden geç geldi.
english: The bus arrived late because of the traffic jam.
tip: yüzünden = 'because of' and marks a bad cause: sıkışıklığı yüzünden = due to the jam. Use it for negative reasons.

target: Bakkaldan ekmek ve süt almayı unutmuşum.
english: I forgot to buy bread and milk from the grocer.
tip: unutmuşum uses -muş in the first person for a realization: 'I've forgotten', softer than the plain unuttum.

target: Bahçemizde beş ağaç ve birçok çiçek var.
english: There are five trees and many flowers in our garden.
tip: After a number the noun stays singular: beş ağaç = five tree(s), never beş ağaçlar. No plural suffix follows a count.

target: Kütüphanede sessiz bir köşe bulup ders çalıştım.
english: I found a quiet corner in the library and studied.
tip: bulup uses -ip to chain two verbs sharing one subject: bul (find) + -up, then çalıştım = 'found ... and studied'.

target: Bize gelen misafirlere çay ve kurabiye ikram ederiz.
english: We offer tea and cookies to guests who come to our house.
tip: gelen turns a verb into an adjective with -en: gel (come) + -en = 'who come', describing misafirlere (the guests).

target: Hakem onu sahadan çıkardı çünkü rakibine sert müdahale etmişti.
english: The referee removed him from the field because he had made a hard tackle on his opponent.
tip: etmişti is the pluperfect (-mişti) = 'had done': the tackle happened before he was sent off, an earlier past.

english: They sell excitedly.
tip: Add -la/-le to a noun to build a manner adverb. heyecan (excitement) becomes heyecanla, meaning with excitement.

english: Do you sometimes want to?
tip: The yes/no word mu stands as its own word, harmonizes, and carries the person ending: istiyor musun means do you want.

english: It is sad that the shop is closing.
tip: The -ma ending turns a verb into a noun. kapanmak (to close) becomes kapanması, the closing of it, with -sı marking whose.
